name: GameChildrensDiscovery
source:
I really like your core idea, as set out in your blurb: the children of people who were stuck inside a fantasy game, not knowing that they're actually in a game. However, I do n't think the concept came across clearly in the story. I was n't sure if Lua, for example, was supposed to know that she was in a game; I did n't think so, but there was a part where she was talking about code malfunctions. 
 
 The concept is really cool and I think you could have an amazing story if Lua et al. slowly discovered the true nature of their world. 
 
 There are a lot of unfamiliar concepts early on that might lead your readers to be confused ( Null, Eden, Sword of Widen, Bag of Holding, plus a lot of place names ). I gather these might be game concepts of some kind but I'm not familiar with them, so it was a little confusing for me. Why, for example, is the sword so important? 
 
 Also, I would think things like `` Thief'' and `` Cleric'' would n't have to be capitalized. My rule of thumb in fantasy is that the more proper nouns you have, the more you risk getting your reader lost. 
 
 Nice work and good luck!
retelling:
Narrated by Lua, the Unknowing Player:

In a world I call home, where the sun rises and sets without my intervention, where rivers flow and mountains stand tall, there lies a truth hidden beneath the surface - a truth I am yet to uncover. This is not just any world; it's a realm where the line between reality and illusion blurs, a place that could very well be a game.

My days are spent in pursuit of survival, seeking shelter from the elements, hunting for food, and avoiding the dangers lurking in every corner. My nights are filled with dreams of a world far removed from this one, a world where my parents reside, perhaps trapped within the very game that has claimed me.

The world around me is teeming with entities not of flesh and blood but of code and lore. A Bag of Holding, an item of mysterious capacity, hangs on my belt, heavy with the weight of secrets yet to be discovered. The Sword of Widen, a weapon of significance I've yet to understand, is always within reach, a constant reminder of the power that lies dormant within me.

I am a Thief, as they call me in this world, and my skills have kept me alive. Yet, I am also something more, something I cannot quite grasp. There are times when the rules of this game seem to bend around me, times when I feel a connection to the very fabric of this reality that goes beyond mere coincidence.

The places I visit, the unnamed towns and forests, are filled with echoes of forgotten tales. Eden and Null are but whispers in the wind, hinting at stories untold and mysteries unsolved. The game's mechanics, the code that governs this world, is a shroud around me, hiding the truth I yearn to find.

I walk this line between ignorance and enlightenment, one foot planted firmly in my reality, the other dangling over the precipice of understanding. I am Lua, the Unknowing Player, seeking answers amidst a world of game terms and place names, clinging to hope that someday I might unlock the secret hidden within this game's code.
